previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of mechanical aortic valve replacement, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, coronary artery disease, peripheral vascular disease, and prior right below-knee amputation was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and hypertensive urgency. She presented with uncontrolled hypertension, elevated troponin likely due to demand ischemia, and an anion gap metabolic acidosis attributed to sodium thiosulfate from dialysis. A CT head revealed a nonspecific medullary hyperdensity, but the patient declined recommended MRI follow-up. She was transferred to Vascular Surgery and underwent a left first and second toe amputation due to dry gangrene, with the procedure scaled down as the gangrene had improved. Her blood pressure was stabilized with a regimen of labetalol, amlodipine, and hydralazine, and anticoagulation was bridged with heparin before restarting warfarin. She recovered well postoperatively, with controlled symptoms and a clean wound, and was discharged home with visiting nurse services for wound care and follow-up appointments in vascular surgery and nephrology.

# New O2 requirement: Mild vascular engorgement and crackles on 
exam suggestive of volume overload as the etiology of her 
hypoxia, improved with ~6L off at HD, infectious workup 
negative, satting well overnight on room air at discharge. 

# Confusion / AMS: Very likely polypharmacy in a patient on 
dialysis, admitted on multiple psychoactive medications 
including zolpidem, gabapentin, ropinarole, lorazepam, 
oxycontin, and hydromorphone, with hydromorphone doses 4mg TID 
and 8mg at night. Hypoxia was also likely contributing. CT head 
with no acute process in ED. Mental status returned to baseline 
with DC'ing ropinarole/gabapentin/lorazepam, decreasing 
oxycontin (see below). Also, discussed the role of oral THC and 
unpredectable rates of absorption.

surgery, patient eager to attempt weaning narcotics. Gabapentin 
was stopped in house without effect. Hydromorphone requirements 
remained ___ q6hrprn. Oxycontin was decreased from 30mg bid to 
20mg bid with good maintenance. I wrote for a weaning protocol 
for oxycontin: 20mg bid for 2 weeks, then 15mg for two weeks 
(script written not to be filled prior to two weeks after 
discharge to ensure insurance coverage, patient educated), then 
10mg bid x2 weeks, then 5mg bid ongoing. Patient in agreement 
and demonstrates good understanding. 

# Nausea/vomiting: etiology unclear, but nausea has been a 
longstanding problem for patient. No diarrhea to suggest 
gastroenteritis, and symptoms have already resolved. Abdomen

101.

hospitalization, metoprolol switched to labetalol which was 
upitrated, other home meds maintained. 

# dCHF: BP aggressively controlled, dialysis as above.

# Restless leg syndrome: Hold home ropinirole, can restart with 
PCP.
